chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he
said regarding the attribute of the Eternal: 'He is One, Self-Sufficient, singular in meaning — not with many different meanings.'

He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: I said, 'May I be your ransom! A group from the people of Iraq allege that He hears with something other than that with which He sees, and He sees with something other than that with which He hears.'

So he (the Imam) said: 'They have lied and deviated and anthropomorphized. Exalted is God above that! He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He hears with that with which He sees, and He sees with that with which He hears.'

He (the narrator) said: I said, 'They allege that He is All-Seeing according to what they themselves comprehend.' So he (the Imam) said: 'Exalted is God! Rather, one comprehends (only) that which has the quality of a creature. And God is not like that.'

key_terms.أَحَدِيُّ الْمَعْنَى: Singular/Unique in meaning — theological term asserting God's attributes are not multiple distinct entities
key_terms.أَلْحَدُوا: They deviated (into heresy/ilhad) — used for those who distort divine attributes
key_terms.الْقَدِيمُ: The Eternal/Pre-existent — divine epithet stressing that God has no beginning
key_terms.سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ: All-Hearing, All-Seeing — divine names from Quran, here interpreted as non-compositional
key_terms.شَبَّهُوا: They anthropomorphized (tashbih) — comparing God to creatures
key_terms.صَمَدٌ: Al-Samad — the Absolute, Self-Sufficient, upon Whom all depend (cf. Quran 112:2)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Baqir explain the oneness of God's hearing and seeing attributes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) addresses a crucial theological dispute about divine attributes, specifically hearing and seeing. Against a group from Iraq who argued these are separate distinct faculties in God (implying multiplicity in the Divine Essence), the Imam firmly rejects this as falsehood, heresy, and anthropomorphism. He teaches that God's hearing and seeing are unified — He hears with the very same faculty by which He sees — affirming God's absolute oneness (tawhid) in His essence and attributes, not merely in number.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeyd, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Regarding the Attribute of the eternality, He<sup>azwj</sup> is One, Solid (not hollow), is in one meaning. It is not with many different meanings’.

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A group from the people of Al-Iraq are alleging that He<sup>azwj</sup> is Hearing with other than what He<sup>azwj</sup> is Seeing (with), and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Seeing with other than what He<sup>azwj</sup> is Hearing (with)?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! They are limiting and resembling (with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>) Exalted is Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from that. He<sup>azwj</sup> is Hearing, Seeing. He<sup>azwj</sup> Hears with what He<sup>azwj</sup> Sees, and Sees with what He<sup>azwj</sup> Hears’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘They are alleging that He<sup>azwj</sup> is Seeing upon what they are comprehending (hearing and seeing to be)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Exalted is Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! But rather, they are (trying to) comprehend with that which is a quality of the creatures, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is not like that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following about being eternal.
“He, Allah, is One, the Self-sufficient. He is One and only One without any multiplicity in different meaning.”

The narrator said that I further inquired, “May Allah take my soul in your service, certain people in Iraq think, that Allah hears with something different from what He sees with, and He sees with something different from what He hears with.”

The Imam replied, “They have said a lie and have become atheists for considering Allah similar to other things. Allah, the Most High, indeed is above all things. He is All-hearing and All-seeing. He hears with what He sees, and sees with what He hears.”

The narrator has said that he further asked, “Those people are also of the opinion that Allah is All-seeing in the same sense and in the same way as they perceive.” The Imam said, “Allah is High Exalted above all such things. Only such things are perceived, which has the attributes of created things. Allah is not created.”
